about: Plain-English healthcare form terms. Lessons, quizzes, and role-plays are all built from these entries. 'say' shows syllables with the stressed part in capitals. 'check' holds two concept-checking questions in the order of the questioning hierarchy (either/or first, then yes/no); they ask about the meaning without using the word itself. 'casas' lists the CASAS competencies the term supports. A teacher should review each entry and set vetted to true. 'confusing' marks words most learners need help with; they are highlighted first on a form. 'tip' tells the learner what to write in that blank, or what to do.

terms.definition: A set amount of money you pay each time you see a doctor or pick up a medicine.
terms.example: My copay for each doctor visit is $20.
terms.tip: Nothing to fill in. It is what you pay at each visit, often at check-in. Your insurance card may list it.

either_or.q: Do you pay it every visit or once a year?

yes_no.q: Is it a set amount, like $20?

terms.definition: The amount you must pay for care each year before your insurance starts to help pay.
terms.example: My deductible is $1,000, so I pay the first $1,000 of my care this year.
terms.tip: Nothing to fill in. Ask your insurance how much of your deductible is left this year.

either_or.q: Do you pay it before or after your insurance starts to help?

yes_no.q: Does it start again every year?

terms.definition: The part of a bill you share with your insurance, shown as a percent, like 20%.
terms.example: My coinsurance is 20%, so I pay $20 when the bill is $100.
terms.tip: Nothing to fill in. Look for a percent, like 20%, on your plan papers.

either_or.q: Is it a percent or a set amount?

yes_no.q: If it is 20%, do you pay $20 of a $100 bill?

terms.definition: The money you pay every month to keep your health insurance.
terms.example: My insurance premium is $150 every month.
terms.tip: Nothing to fill in. You pay it to your insurance company each month, not to the clinic.

either_or.q: Do you pay it every month or only when you see a doctor?
options: only when you see a doctor

yes_no.q: Do you pay it to keep your insurance?

terms.definition: The most money you will have to pay for covered care in one year.
terms.example: After I reach my out-of-pocket maximum, my insurance pays for the rest of my covered care this year.
terms.tip: Nothing to fill in. Your plan papers show this number for the year.

either_or.q: Is it the most or the least you pay in a year?

yes_no.q: After you reach it, does your insurance pay for the rest of your covered care?

terms.definition: A card from your health plan that shows your name and your plan numbers.
terms.example: Please show your insurance card at the front desk.
terms.tip: Bring it to every visit. The front desk may copy the front and back.

either_or.q: Do you get it from your health plan or from the pharmacy?

yes_no.q: Does it show your name?

terms.definition: The number on your insurance card that shows who you are to your health plan.
terms.example: Write the member ID from the front of your card.
terms.tip: Copy the member ID from the front of your insurance card, letter by letter.

either_or.q: Is it a number or a name?

yes_no.q: Is it on your insurance card?

terms.definition: The number on your insurance card for your plan, often the plan from your job.
terms.example: The group number is under my name on the card.
terms.tip: Copy the group number from your insurance card. If your card has none, write N/A.

either_or.q: Is it a number for your plan or for your doctor?

yes_no.q: Is it often for a plan from your job?

terms.definition: The person whose name the health insurance plan is under.
terms.example: My husband is the policyholder because the insurance comes from his job.
terms.tip: Write the name of the person the insurance is under. If it is your own plan, write your name.

either_or.q: Is it a person or a number?

yes_no.q: Is the health plan under this person's name?

terms.definition: Your main health plan, the one that pays first.
terms.example: My primary insurance is from my job, so they pay first.
terms.tip: Write the name of your main insurance plan, the way it is printed on your card.

either_or.q: Does it pay first or second?

yes_no.q: Is it your main plan?

terms.definition: A second health plan that can help pay what your first plan does not pay.
terms.example: I have secondary insurance through my wife's job.
terms.tip: Write your second plan if you have one. If you don't, write N/A.

either_or.q: Is it your first plan or your second plan?

yes_no.q: Can it help pay what the first plan does not pay?

terms.definition: Doctors and hospitals that have a deal with your insurance, so care costs you less.
terms.example: This clinic is in-network, so my visit costs less.
terms.tip: Nothing to fill in. Before a visit, ask: Are you in-network with my plan?

either_or.q: Does care there usually cost less or more?

yes_no.q: Does the doctor have a deal with your insurance?

terms.definition: Doctors and hospitals that do not have a deal with your insurance, so care often costs more.
terms.example: That hospital is out-of-network, so I might get a bigger bill.
terms.tip: Nothing to fill in. Ask before a visit, because it can cost more.

either_or.q: Does care there often cost less or more?

yes_no.q: Does the doctor have a deal with your insurance?

terms.definition: A bill that is sent to your insurance company to ask them to pay for your care.
terms.example: The clinic sent a claim to my insurance after my visit.
terms.tip: Nothing to fill in. The clinic usually sends it to your insurance for you.

either_or.q: Is it sent to your insurance or to your pharmacy?

yes_no.q: Does it ask the insurance company to pay?

terms.definition: A paper from your insurance that shows what they paid and what you may owe; it is not a bill.
terms.example: My Explanation of Benefits says my insurance paid $80 for my visit.
terms.tip: Keep it with your bills, and compare the two before you pay anything.

either_or.q: Does it come from your insurance or from your pharmacy?

yes_no.q: Is it a bill?

terms.definition: Permission your insurance must give before you get some tests, medicines, or treatments.
terms.example: My MRI needs prior authorization from my insurance first.
terms.tip: Nothing to fill in. Your doctor's office usually asks your insurance for it.

either_or.q: Do you need it before or after the test?

yes_no.q: Does your insurance give it?

terms.definition: A note from your main doctor that sends you to see a different, special doctor.
terms.example: I need a referral to see a heart doctor.
terms.tip: If the form asks who referred you, write the name of the doctor who sent you.

either_or.q: Does it come from your main doctor or from the pharmacy?

yes_no.q: Does it send you to a different doctor?

terms.definition: California's free or low-cost health insurance for people with low income.
terms.example: My children have Medi-Cal, so their visits do not cost money.
terms.tip: If you have Medi-Cal, copy the ID number from your Medi-Cal card.

either_or.q: Is it a health plan or a doctor's name?

yes_no.q: Is it free or low-cost?

terms.definition: Health insurance from the U.S. government for people 65 or older and some people with disabilities.
terms.example: My grandmother uses Medicare to pay for her doctor visits.
terms.tip: If you have Medicare, copy the number from your Medicare card.

either_or.q: Is it mostly for people 65 and older or for children?

yes_no.q: Is it from the U.S. government?

terms.definition: The money you still need to pay on a bill.
terms.example: The balance due on my bill is $35.
terms.tip: This is what you still owe. Call the billing office if it looks wrong.

either_or.q: Is it money you still owe or money you already paid?

yes_no.q: Do you need to pay it?

terms.definition: A way to pay a big bill in small parts, a little each month.
terms.example: I set up a payment plan to pay $30 each month.
terms.tip: If a bill is too big to pay at once, call the billing office and ask for one.

either_or.q: Do you pay a little each month or all at once?

yes_no.q: Is it for a big bill?

terms.definition: The phone line for your health plan that answers questions about your coverage.
terms.example: I called member services to ask if my doctor is in-network.
terms.tip: The phone number is usually on the back of your insurance card.

either_or.q: Is it a phone line or a clinic?

yes_no.q: Can it answer questions about your plan?

terms.definition: The person who agrees to pay the bill, like a parent paying for a child.
terms.example: I am the guarantor for my son's doctor bills.
terms.tip: Write the name of the person who will pay the bill. For most adults, that is you.

either_or.q: Is it a person or a place?

yes_no.q: Does this person agree to pay the bill?

terms.definition: Paying for care with your own money, without using insurance.
terms.example: I do not have insurance, so I am self-pay.
terms.tip: Check this box only if you will pay without insurance.

either_or.q: Do you pay with your own money or with insurance?

yes_no.q: Do you use insurance?

terms.definition: An agreement that you will pay any part of the bill your insurance does not pay.
terms.example: I signed the financial responsibility form at the front desk.
terms.tip: Read it, then sign. It means you will pay what your insurance does not.

either_or.q: Is it about paying or about medicine?

yes_no.q: Do you agree to pay what insurance does not pay?

terms.definition: Permission for your insurance to send payment straight to the doctor's office instead of to you.
terms.example: The assignment of benefits lets my insurance pay the clinic directly.
terms.tip: Read it, then sign. It lets your insurance pay the clinic directly.

either_or.q: Does the insurance pay the doctor's office or you?

yes_no.q: Do you give permission?

terms.definition: Your main doctor, who you see for checkups and common health problems.
terms.example: My primary care provider is Dr. Lee.
terms.tip: Write the name of your main doctor. If you don't have one, write none.

either_or.q: Is it your main doctor or a special doctor?

yes_no.q: Do you see this doctor for common health problems?

terms.definition: A doctor who knows a lot about one part of the body or one kind of illness.
terms.example: My doctor sent me to a specialist for my skin.
terms.tip: If the form asks, write the name of the special doctor you see.

either_or.q: Does this doctor know a lot about one part of the body or about everything?

yes_no.q: Is a heart doctor one?

terms.definition: A clinic for problems that need care today but are not life-threatening, like a bad cold or a small cut.
terms.example: I went to urgent care for my hurt ankle.
terms.tip: Nothing to fill in. Go here for problems that can't wait but are not emergencies.

either_or.q: Is it for a bad cold or for chest pain?

yes_no.q: Is it for life-threatening problems?

terms.definition: The hospital area for very serious problems, like chest pain or trouble breathing.
terms.example: Go to the emergency room or call 911 if you have chest pain.
terms.tip: Nothing to fill in. For chest pain or trouble breathing, call 911.

either_or.q: Is it for a small cut or for trouble breathing?

yes_no.q: Is it in a hospital?

terms.definition: A set day and time to see a doctor or nurse.
terms.example: My appointment is on Monday at 9:00 a.m.
terms.tip: Write the date and time of your visit, like 11/03 at 9:00 a.m.

either_or.q: Is it a day and time or a place?

yes_no.q: Do you plan it before you see the doctor?

terms.definition: Telling the front desk you have arrived and giving them your information.
terms.example: Please come 15 minutes early for check-in.
terms.tip: Come a little early and bring your insurance card and a photo ID.

either_or.q: Do you do it when you arrive or when you leave?

yes_no.q: Do you do it at the front desk?

terms.definition: Another visit after your first one, so the doctor can check how you are doing.
terms.example: The doctor wants a follow-up visit in two weeks.
terms.tip: Before you leave, ask the front desk to schedule it.

either_or.q: Is it your first visit or a visit after that?

yes_no.q: Does the doctor check how you are doing?

terms.definition: A visit once a year to check your health, even when you are not sick.
terms.example: I get my annual physical every January.
terms.tip: Nothing to fill in. Ask your insurance if it is covered.

either_or.q: Is it once a year or once a week?

yes_no.q: Do you need to be sick to go?

terms.definition: Seeing a doctor by video or phone instead of going to the office.
terms.example: I had a telehealth visit on my phone.
terms.tip: If the form asks, choose whether you want a video visit or a phone visit.

either_or.q: Do you see the doctor on a screen or in the office?

yes_no.q: Can you do it on your phone?

terms.definition: A person who helps you talk with the doctor in your language, usually for free.
terms.example: I asked for an interpreter for my appointment.
terms.tip: Check yes if you want one. It is usually free.

either_or.q: Is it a person or a paper?

yes_no.q: Does this person help you talk with the doctor in your language?

terms.definition: The rules about what happens, like a fee, if you miss a visit or cancel too late.
terms.example: The cancellation policy says to call one day before if you cannot come.
terms.tip: Read it. Call ahead if you can't come, so you are not charged a fee.

either_or.q: Is it about missing a visit or about medicine?

yes_no.q: Can there be a fee if you cancel too late?

terms.definition: The main health problem or need that brought you to the doctor today.
terms.example: My reason for visit is a cough that will not go away.
terms.tip: Write your main problem in a few words, like: cough for two weeks.

either_or.q: Is it your health problem today or your address?

yes_no.q: Can a cough be the answer?

terms.definition: Someone who has never seen this doctor or clinic before.
terms.example: I filled out a new patient form at my first visit.
terms.tip: Check yes if this is your first visit to this clinic.

either_or.q: Is it your first time here or your tenth time?

yes_no.q: Have you seen this doctor before?

terms.definition: A website or app where you can see test results, send messages to your doctor, and make visits.
terms.example: I can see my test results on the patient portal.
terms.tip: If you want to see your results online, write your email address.

either_or.q: Is it a website or a building?

yes_no.q: Can you see test results there?

terms.definition: A check of your blood, urine, or other samples to learn about your health.
terms.example: The doctor ordered a lab test to check my blood sugar.
terms.tip: Nothing to fill in. The doctor tells you if you need one.

either_or.q: Does it check your blood or your insurance?

yes_no.q: Can it check your blood sugar?

terms.definition: The day, month, and year you were born.
terms.example: Write your date of birth like this: 03/15/1985.
terms.tip: Write the month, day, and year in numbers, like 03/15/1985.

either_or.q: Is it the day you were born or today's date?

yes_no.q: Does it have a year?

terms.definition: The street, city, and ZIP code where you get your mail.
terms.example: Write your mailing address so the clinic can send you letters.
terms.tip: Write your street, city, state, and ZIP code.

either_or.q: Is it where you get mail or your phone number?

yes_no.q: Does it have a ZIP code?

terms.definition: A person the clinic can call if something serious happens to you.
terms.example: I put my sister as my emergency contact.
terms.tip: Write the name and phone number of someone you trust. It can't be you.

either_or.q: Is it a person or a hospital?

yes_no.q: Will the clinic call this person if something serious happens?

terms.definition: How a person is connected to you, like mother, husband, or friend.
terms.example: Next to relationship to patient, I wrote daughter.
terms.tip: Write how that person is related to you, like sister or friend.

either_or.q: Is the answer 'sister' or '555-1234'?

yes_no.q: Can the answer be 'friend'?

terms.definition: Your name written by hand in your own way to show you agree.
terms.example: Put your signature at the bottom of the page.
terms.tip: Sign your name the way you usually do.

either_or.q: Do you write it by hand or type a number?

yes_no.q: Does it show that you agree?

terms.definition: An adult who has the legal right to make decisions for a child or another person.
terms.example: A parent or legal guardian must sign for children under 18.
terms.tip: Only for patients under 18. If you are an adult filling it out for yourself, leave it blank.

either_or.q: Is it an adult or a child?

yes_no.q: Can this person make decisions for a child?

terms.definition: The language you want to use when you talk with the doctor and read papers.
terms.example: I wrote my preferred language on the form so they can call an interpreter.
terms.tip: Write the language you speak best.

either_or.q: Is the answer 'Spanish' or 'Monday'?

yes_no.q: Can it help the clinic get you someone who speaks your language?

terms.definition: Whether you are single, married, divorced, or widowed.
terms.example: For marital status, I checked married.
terms.tip: Check one box: single, married, divorced, or widowed.

either_or.q: Is the answer 'married' or 'tall'?

yes_no.q: Can the answer be 'single'?

terms.definition: Something you write when a question is not about you or your situation.
terms.example: I do not have a second insurance, so I wrote N/A.
terms.tip: Write N/A when a question is not about you, instead of leaving it blank.

either_or.q: Do you write it when a question is about you or not about you?

yes_no.q: If you have no second insurance, can you write it?

terms.definition: The number the clinic uses to find your health file.
terms.example: The clinic uses my medical record number to find my file.
terms.tip: Leave it blank. The clinic fills it in.

either_or.q: Is it a number or a name?

yes_no.q: Does the clinic use it to find your file?

terms.definition: Foods, medicines, plants, or other things that make your body react badly, like a rash or swelling.
terms.example: I have allergies to peanuts and penicillin.
terms.tip: List medicines, foods, or other things you are allergic to. If none, write none.

either_or.q: Do they make your body react badly or feel better?

yes_no.q: Can a food cause one?

terms.definition: Information about your past illnesses, health problems, and treatments.
terms.example: The doctor asked about my medical history.
terms.tip: List illnesses you have had and treatments you have received.

either_or.q: Is it about your past or about your bill?

yes_no.q: Does it include illnesses you had before?

terms.definition: Health problems that your parents, brothers, sisters, or grandparents have had.
terms.example: Diabetes is in my family history because my mother has it.
terms.tip: List health problems your parents, brothers, or sisters have had.

either_or.q: Is it about your parents' health or your job?

yes_no.q: If your mother has diabetes, do you write it here?

terms.definition: Changes in your body that show you may be sick, like fever, pain, or cough.
terms.example: My symptoms are a sore throat and a fever.
terms.tip: Write what you feel, like fever, cough, or pain.

either_or.q: Is a fever one, or is a bill one?

yes_no.q: Can pain be one?

terms.definition: The name the doctor gives to your illness or health problem after checking you.
terms.example: The diagnosis was an ear infection.
terms.tip: Nothing to fill in. The doctor writes it after checking you.

either_or.q: Does the doctor give it or the front desk?

yes_no.q: Is it the name of your health problem?

terms.definition: A health problem that lasts a long time, like diabetes or high blood pressure.
terms.example: High blood pressure is a chronic condition.
terms.tip: Check any long-term health problem you have, like diabetes or high blood pressure.

either_or.q: Does it last a long time or one day?

yes_no.q: Is high blood pressure one?

terms.definition: Treatment where a doctor opens part of your body to fix a problem, usually in a hospital.
terms.example: I had surgery on my knee in 2019.
terms.tip: List any operations you have had and the year of each one.

either_or.q: Is it usually in a hospital or at a pharmacy?

yes_no.q: Does a doctor open part of your body?

terms.definition: Medicine, usually given with a needle, that protects you from certain diseases, like the flu.
terms.example: My son needs his immunizations before school starts.
terms.tip: Write the shots you have had, or bring your vaccine record.

either_or.q: Are they usually given with a needle or by phone?

yes_no.q: Do they protect you from some diseases?

terms.definition: Whether you smoke cigarettes, vape, or use chewing products.
terms.example: The form asks about tobacco use, so I checked never.
terms.tip: Answer honestly, so the doctor can help you.

either_or.q: Is it about cigarettes or about sleep?

yes_no.q: Does vaping count?

terms.definition: All the medicines, vitamins, and pills you take now.
terms.example: Bring a list of your current medications to every visit.
terms.tip: List every medicine, vitamin, and pill you take now. Bring the bottles if you can.

either_or.q: Is it medicine you take now or medicine you took years ago?

yes_no.q: Do vitamins go on this list?

terms.definition: A doctor's written order for a medicine you can only get from a pharmacy.
terms.example: The doctor sent my prescription to the pharmacy.
terms.tip: Nothing to fill in. The doctor sends it to your pharmacy.

either_or.q: Does a doctor write it or a store?

yes_no.q: Do you get the medicine from a pharmacy?

terms.definition: How much medicine to take and how often to take it.
terms.example: The dosage is one pill two times a day.
terms.tip: Read the label: how much to take, and how often.

either_or.q: Is it how much medicine or how much money?

yes_no.q: Does it say how often to take the medicine?

terms.definition: Getting more of the same medicine after you finish it.
terms.example: I called the pharmacy for a refill.
terms.tip: Check the label to see how many refills you have left.

either_or.q: Is it more of the same medicine or a new medicine?

yes_no.q: Do you get it after you finish your medicine?

terms.definition: A store where you pick up your medicine.
terms.example: My pharmacy is the one near my house.
terms.tip: Write the name and street of the pharmacy you use.

either_or.q: Is it a store or a doctor?

yes_no.q: Do you pick up medicine there?

terms.definition: A cheaper medicine that works the same as the brand-name one.
terms.example: The generic drug costs $4 instead of $40.
terms.tip: You can ask the pharmacist: Is there a generic?

either_or.q: Is it cheaper or more expensive?

yes_no.q: Does it work the same as the brand-name medicine?

terms.definition: An unwanted change in your body from a medicine, like feeling sleepy or sick.
terms.example: One side effect of this medicine is a dry mouth.
terms.tip: Tell the doctor or pharmacist if you notice any.

either_or.q: Is it a change you want or a change you don't want?

yes_no.q: Can feeling sleepy be one?

terms.definition: Medicine you can buy at a store without a doctor's note, like many pain pills.
terms.example: I take an over-the-counter medicine for headaches.
terms.tip: List these too when the form asks about your medicines.

either_or.q: Do you need a doctor's note or not?
options: you don't need a doctor's note
either_or.answer: you don't need a doctor's note

yes_no.q: Can you buy it at a store?

terms.definition: Vitamins, herbs, or other products you take to stay healthy that are not medicine from a doctor.
terms.example: Please list any supplements you take, like fish oil.
terms.tip: List vitamins and herbs you take, like fish oil.

either_or.q: Are they vitamins or bills?

yes_no.q: Are they medicine from a doctor?

terms.definition: Saying yes, usually by signing, that you agree to a treatment or test.
terms.example: I signed a consent form before my blood test.
terms.tip: Read it, ask questions, then sign if you agree.

either_or.q: Does it mean yes or no?

yes_no.q: Do you usually sign for it?

terms.definition: A paper that explains how the clinic keeps your health information private and who can see it.
terms.example: The front desk gave me a Notice of Privacy Practices to read.
terms.tip: Read it, then sign to show you received it.

either_or.q: Is it about keeping your information safe or about paying?

yes_no.q: Does it say who can see your health information?

aliases: authorization for release of health information
terms.definition: Your permission for the clinic to share your health records with another person or office.
terms.example: I signed a release of information so my new doctor can see my records.
terms.tip: Write who can get your records, then sign.

either_or.q: Does it let the clinic share your records or delete them?

yes_no.q: Do you give permission?

terms.definition: A paper that says what care you want, and who will decide for you, if you become too sick to speak.
terms.example: The hospital asked if I have an advance directive.
terms.tip: Check yes or no. If you don't have one, you can ask the clinic about it.

either_or.q: Is it for when you are too sick to speak or for when you are healthy?
options: when you are too sick to speak
either_or.answer: when you are too sick to speak

yes_no.q: Does it say who decides for you?
